constraints_found.constraint: Liam craves a burger, not noodles
constraints_found.source_line: liam: "and before you say it, no, not noodles today. i want a BURGER. big and messy"

constraints_found.constraint: Must be quick: Mina has a 1:15 critique, so no long sit-down meal
constraints_found.source_line: mina: "the only thing is my studio critique starts at 1:15, so i can't stay long. sorry" / liam: "so we grab it fast and go. no long sit-down thing. got it"

constraints_found.constraint: Mina needs a real vegetarian burger (veggie patty), not just fries. Implies she is vegetarian, which rules out a place where even the fries are cooked in beef fat
constraints_found.source_line: mina: "...that's really sweet of you. a veggie patty would make my whole day" (supported by liam: "this time you get a real burger too. one you can actually eat, not just the sides")

constraints_found.constraint: Budget: cheap student lunch implied; all venues are $, so it never decides the pick
constraints_found.source_line: No explicit line; inferred from campus/student context

elimination.campus_brisket_box: Fast and cheap, but meat only, and the fries are cooked in beef fat. Nothing Mina can eat.
elimination.campus_patty_parlor: Has a veggie patty, but it is slow table service ('Don't come here on a short break'). Fails the time limit.
elimination.campus_noodle_cellar: Fast and veggie-friendly, but noodles only. Liam explicitly said no noodles.
elimination.campus_bun_stop: Counter service, five minutes, cheap, black bean patty. Meets every constraint.

notes: Clean three-constraint elimination puzzle, and each decoy fails on exactly one constraint. That is a good design.

Mina's vegetarianism is never stated outright. The player infers it from 'i can always just get fries', 'one you can actually eat' and 'veggie patty'. That is fair, but a first-time player could read it as a preference rather than a strict diet. It makes no difference here, because Brisket Box fails either way.
Budget is never mentioned, and all four venues are $, so price plays no part.
The 'mina can just get fries' line is a nice trap. Taken at face value it would make Brisket Box look acceptable, and its review deliberately closes that loophole (beef-fat fries).
